title: 1990'S COMPAQ PERSONAL PORTABL...
reason: Compaq's first laptop (SLT/286) with detachable keyboard, original bag and adapter, collected by retro computing buyers; my estimate about $100 to $250 depending on whether it works.
findings: Compaq SLT/286 portable computer (badge legible on the lid in photo 3: COMPAQ SLT/286 with the red, orange and yellow stripe). Supplied with its detachable keyboard on a coiled cable (photo 4), a black Compaq carry bag (stripe emblem on the front flap, COMPAQ printed on the lining), a white AC adapter with vent slots, a grey mains lead and other leads in the bag (photo 6). The front shows a 3.5 inch floppy drive slot and a second drive-style panel; the keyboard has legible legends and a function key row. No serial or model plate is visible (underside not shown) and the adapter's small blue label is unreadable. The screen is off in every photo and the title says AS IS, so working order is unknown. The SLT/286 was launched in 1988 (Wikipedia, checked 19/10/2026: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compaq_SLT) as Compaq's first laptop and the first with a backlit VGA LCD, so the title's 1990's is loose.
condition: Beige case is yellowed and grubby with scuffs; keys look yellowed but intact; small brown spot on the lid badge panel; the bag is dusty and worn with a scuffed handle and strap. Screen condition (bleed, backlight), battery pack and hard drive not shown or tested.
rescore_note: Genuine Compaq SLT/286 (badge legible, launched 1988) with detachable keyboard, original bag, adapter and mains lead, which retro computing buyers like, but it is sold AS IS and untested with a yellowed case and no battery shown, and flat clock batteries and dead hard drives are commonly reported faults, so the realistic mix of working and dead is about AU$100 to $200 (working units list for a few hundred dollars and dead ones for very little; no dated sold prices verified).
